title: Interpret Layer Count and Logic ID fields on the Container Selection screen (single-density site; Logic ID not used)
summary: Use the Container Selection screen fields “Layer Count” and “Logic ID” to interpret what the screen is showing for this single-density site: Layer Count should indicate one layer, and Logic ID is displayed but not used operationally in this environment.
when_to_use: When you need to interpret what the Container Selection screen is indicating for rack/container configuration on a single-density site, specifically the meaning of the “Layer Count” and whether “Logic ID” should be treated as operationally meaningful.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Interpret the “Layer Count” and “Logic ID” fields on the Container Selection screen according to this site’s single-density configuration and the stated Logic ID usage note.
access_or_tools_needed: Visibility of the “Layer Count” and “Logic ID” fields

access_required: Access to the Container Selection screen (HMI)
system_preconditions: This interpretation applies to the single-density rack configuration described in the source (only one layer used).

visual_references.description: Training video frame showing the Container Selection screen context where the “Layer Count” and “Logic ID” fields are discussed (single-density racks => one layer; Logic ID not used).

steps.title: Open the Container Selection screen and locate the fields labeled “Layer Count” and “Logic ID”.
steps.purpose: Identify the exact fields on the Container Selection screen that must be interpreted for this site configuration.
steps.instruction: Open the Container Selection screen and find the on-screen fields labeled “Layer Count” and “Logic ID”.
steps.expected_result: You can visually locate both “Layer Count” and “Logic ID” on the Container Selection screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Both field labels are visible and readable on the Container Selection screen.
steps.failure_condition: One or both fields are not visible (e.g., screen is not on the correct view, or the UI is not displaying the expected container details).

actions.label: Locate Layer Count and Logic ID fields
actions.exact_action: Locate the fields labeled “Layer Count” and “Logic ID”.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The segment discusses the three things “Logic ID, layer count and don't count again” and references the Container Selection screen context.

steps.title: Interpret Layer Count using the site’s single-density rack configuration (Layer Count should be one layer).
steps.purpose: Correctly interpret what “Layer Count” means for this single-density site so you don’t misread the rack/container configuration.
steps.instruction: Interpret “Layer Count” as reflecting the rack property configuration. For this site, racks are single density, so only one layer is used; therefore “Layer Count” should be consistent with one layer.
steps.expected_result: The “Layer Count” value you see corresponds to a single layer (one layer) for this site’s single-density racks.
steps.healthy_condition: “Layer Count” indicates one layer, consistent with the site being single density (“we only have one layer… we don’t have multiple layers”).
steps.failure_condition: “Layer Count” indicates multiple layers (i.e., not consistent with single-density => not one layer).

actions.label: Check Layer Count matches single-density (one layer)
actions.exact_action: Interpret Layer Count … confirm that the site uses single density racks so Layer Count is effectively one layer.

stop_or_escalate_if: If “Layer Count” indicates multiple layers (contrary to the single-density interpretation), stop and escalate for clarification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “all our shelves or reacts are single density show. So we only have one layer. We we don't have multiple layers… Logic ID, layer count… we put in one layer… we only have one.”
Layer Count on the screen reflects rack configuration… this site uses a single layer.

steps.title: Interpret Logic ID as not used in this deployment.
steps.purpose: Avoid treating “Logic ID” as operationally meaningful when it is explicitly stated as not used in this environment.
steps.instruction: Treat the “Logic ID” field as displayed but not used operationally for this site’s operations. When reporting findings, do not base operational conclusions on Logic ID for this environment.
steps.expected_result: You disregard “Logic ID” for operational interpretation because it is not used in this deployment.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation/reporting focuses on Layer Count (single-density => one layer) and does not rely on Logic ID as an operational control/meaning.
steps.failure_condition: You treat “Logic ID” as operationally meaningful contrary to the stated usage note.

actions.label: Confirm Logic ID is not used operationally
actions.exact_action: Interpret Logic ID using the source’s usage note: treat Logic ID as not used in this deployment.

stop_or_escalate_if: If Logic ID appears to be used operationally contrary to the source’s usage note, stop and escalate for clarification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “we don't use the logic ID” and “what is there? … Logic ID, layer count … we don't use the logic ID”.
Logic ID appears on the container-related screen, but the training says this field is not used in this deployment.

steps.title: Report findings using the correct interpretation (Layer Count consistent with one layer; Logic ID not used).
steps.purpose: Ensure communications reflect the correct operational interpretation for this site configuration.
steps.instruction: When you report what the Container Selection screen is showing, include that Layer Count should be consistent with single-density (one layer) and that Logic ID is not used for this site’s operations.
steps.expected_result: Your report states Layer Count is one layer for this single-density site and that Logic ID is not used operationally.
steps.healthy_condition: The report aligns with the single-density interpretation and explicitly does not treat Logic ID as operationally meaningful.
steps.failure_condition: The report claims Logic ID is used operationally or contradicts the single-density expectation for Layer Count.

actions.label: State correct interpretation in findings
actions.exact_action: Include that Layer Count should be consistent with single-density (one layer) and that Logic ID is not used for this site’s operations.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Segment states racks are single density (“only one layer… don’t have multiple layers”) and “we don’t use the logic ID”.

success_criteria: Layer Count is interpreted as one layer for this single-density site configuration.
Logic ID is treated as not used operationally when interpreting the Container Selection screen.
healthy_conditions: “Layer Count” matches the single-density expectation (one layer).
“Logic ID” is not used as a basis for operational interpretation in this environment.
failure_conditions: “Layer Count” indicates multiple layers (inconsistent with single-density => one layer).
Logic ID is treated as operationally meaningful contrary to the stated usage note.
escalation_guidance: If “Layer Count” indicates multiple layers or if “Logic ID” appears to be used operationally contrary to the source’s usage note, stop and escalate for clarification.
